correctness.rationale: A 3-cycle of a nonconstant binary triple swaps the unique minority bit with another of the two positions, equivalent exactly to exchanging unequal bits at distance 1 or 2; every such edge can be realized by some length-three window even at n=3. Thus the move graph is the k-token graph of the squared path. For any connected base graph, token-slide distance equals min-cost integral transshipment: a directed acyclic optimum has an occupied→unoccupied positive-flow arc whenever the current set differs from target, and this reduces divergence and flow cost by 1. Integral LP duality gives max signed sum of integer edge-1-Lipschitz potentials. Removing any one vertex from P_n^2 leaves it connected, so sorted potential gaps δ_i∈{0,1} cannot have adjacent ones. Summing k windows of m=n-k gaps gives <=ceil(km/2); integer potentials floor((j-1)/2),ceil((j-1)/2) attain it for extreme initial/final blocks. Independent BFS and min-matching tests confirmed all 66,174 ordered word pairs n=3..9; this is evidence, not proof for arbitrary n.

value.rationale: The exact diameter is the natural worst-case number of sequential length-three cyclic-permutation bursts at fixed binary composition, with an explicit diametral pair and a transport proof. This addresses global reachability/metric complexity of a previously motivated burst channel, not a re-run of single-burst code tables.

final_claim: For every binary word length n>=3 and nontrivial weight 1<=k<n, the graph under sequential rotations of contiguous length-three windows is F_k(P_n^2), connected, with exact diameter ceil(k(n-k)/2), attained by 1^k0^(n-k) and its reversal.
limitations: Binary fixed-weight words, n>=3, sequential rotations of contiguous triples with no wraparound; no code-size result, no longer windows, no nonbinary channel.
BFS through n=9 is finite corroboration only; min-flow dual and sorted-potential upper bound prove unrestricted formula.
